newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Chile sees free trade deal with Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Chile sees free trade deal with Mexico.

text.p: Chile, Latin America's strongest economy, plans to conclude a free trade agreement with Mexico by November along similar lines to its recent deal with Canada, Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza said on Thursday.
"We have an agreement very similar to the one like NAFTA with Canada. We are concluding one with Mexico before November, we hope on similar terms," Insulza told reporters.
Insulza was on a four-day official visit to Singapore and held discussions with senior leaders in the city-state including Prime Minister Goh Tok Chong.

The Chilean Senate gave final approval on Wednesday to a free trade agreement with Canada, putting the treaty into effect and laying the groundwork for Chile's long-delayed entrance into the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA).
Insulza said Chile, whose entry into NAFTA has been stalled in the U.S. Congress, could now actively examine one of two possibilities in its trading relationship with the U.S.
"One is still joining NAFTA and another one would be to sign a bilateral free trade agreement with the United States on more or less similar terms as we have with Mexico and Canada."
Insulza told a questioner that Chile had not heard any response from the United States on NAFTA. "This is a process which has taken much longer than we expected."
Chile's agreement with Canada sweeps away tariffs on about 80 percent of trade between the two countries immediately and will phase out the rest over the next 18 years.
Chilean officials have said the treaty could boost bilateral trade, currently at about $670 million a year, five-fold over the next decade.
Analysts said the treaty's main impact might be to set the basic terms for Chile's later inclusion in NAFTA as its fourth partner after the United States, Mexico and Canada.
